curriculumTitle: Understanding Earth's Dynamic Systems: The Afar Region
subject: Earth Science
centralPhenomenon: Earthquake and crustal cracking in the Afar region (2005)
description: A phenomenon-based unit exploring plate tectonics, mantle convection, and Earth's dynamic systems through investigation of the Afar region

parts.partSubtitle: Understanding how forces create stability and change in Earth systems

units.title: What is happening in the Afar region?
units.coreIdea: Earthquakes occur along patterns related to plate boundaries and faults, causing surface cracking and movement.
units.drivingQuestion: What is happening in the Afar region?
units.phenomenon: Students read about an earthquake in the Afar region, explore global earthquake maps, and develop initial models
keyContent: A crack opened up in Earth's crust in 2005 in the Afar region
Earthquakes seem to happen mostly along plate boundaries, but some happen in the middle of plates
They all seem to be connected to faults
Earthquakes happen underground and can cause cracking and moving of Earth's surface
units.navigation: What is actually causing the ground to shake and break? Why do all earthquakes not result in breaks?
performanceExpectations: Develop a diagrammatic model of relationships between Earth systems to explain what causes land to crack, break, and move
Ask questions about mechanisms driving changes in Earth's crust from careful observation of patterns

units.title: Forces and System Stability
units.coreIdea: Systems remain stable when forces are balanced, but sudden changes occur when forces become unbalanced.
units.drivingQuestion: What allows a system to remain stable when forces are acting on it, and what causes it to suddenly change?
units.phenomenon: Foam models simulating plate motions, spring scales modeling equilibrium forces, free-body diagrams
keyContent: All systems change; 'stability' is dependent on scale
Objects in contact exert contact forces
Concept of 'net force' and that it is zero when forces balance
Vectors in 2-dimension can be separated into components
Large-scale changes in Earth's structure can result from a combination of forces
units.navigation: What happens if forces in foam simulation increase? Brainstorm other investigations to do in next lesson.
performanceExpectations: Plan and conduct an investigation to determine contact force interactions that result in observed stability and change
Develop and use free-body diagrams to explain and predict how force magnitude impacts system stability

units.title: Matter and Energy Changes Under Force
units.coreIdea: When balanced forces increase in magnitude, matter deforms elastically until it reaches its limit and permanently changes.
units.drivingQuestion: What happens to the matter and energy in a system when the magnitude of balanced forces on it increases?
units.phenomenon: Foam experiments with multiple force configurations, energy transfer analysis
keyContent: Changes in matter and energy transfers happen together
Unbalanced forces transfer energy
All solid materials deform elastically when force is applied, up to a point
When solids deform past their elastic limit, they permanently deform including cracks and breaking
units.navigation: How do unbalanced forces lead to deformation?
performanceExpectations: Make qualitative claims about how force magnitude differences affect material structure and energy transfer
Ask questions about energy transfer and storage in deformed matter

units.title: Particle-Level Changes in Deformation
units.coreIdea: At the particle level, external forces create imbalances between particles, leading to movement until forces rebalance or bonds break.
units.drivingQuestion: What is changing in the matter at a particle level before an earthquake, and when a solid elastically deforms or breaks?
units.phenomenon: Magnetic particle simulations, computational models of deformation and breaking
keyContent: External forces create temporary imbalances between particles
In elastic deformation, particles move until forces are balanced
All changes in matter are changes in motion--either large scale or at particle level
If unbalanced forces deform a solid too much, particle bonds break
Matter produces fields that exert forces across distances, energy can be transferred to, from, and stored in fields
units.navigation: Poll if need more data to explain Afar--should state that since it didn't happen at a plate boundary, need more information
performanceExpectations: Evaluate merits and limitations of different models for understanding earthquakes and deformation
Use computational models to explore stability, change, and cause-effect relationships between forces and matter

parts.partSubtitle: Investigating how Earth's internal structure and energy drive surface processes

units.title: Investigating Earth's Interior
units.coreIdea: Seismic wave data provide evidence that Earth has layered structure with different materials affecting surface features.
units.drivingQuestion: How do we investigate the connection between matter in Earth's interior and surface features above?
units.phenomenon: Seismic wave data analysis, Earth layer modeling, mantle comparison between Afar and local regions
keyContent: Wave speed through matter depends on the matter through which it passes
Seismic velocity data provide evidence that Earth is composed of layers
Earth has a solid inner core, liquid outer core, mantle, and crust
Differences in mantle matter cause unbalanced forces in different locations
units.navigation: Exit slip about student knowledge of how different temperatures of flowing matter move/interact
performanceExpectations: Analyze mathematical representations of seismic data to reveal patterns in wave arrival times
Analyze seismic velocity anomaly data to provide evidence for causal links between mantle variation and surface features

units.title: Temperature and Mantle Behavior
units.coreIdea: Temperature increases are associated with increased molecular movement, driving matter cycling in Earth's interior through convection.
units.drivingQuestion: How is temperature related to behavior of matter in the mantle?
units.phenomenon: Temperature data analysis, convection tank observations
keyContent: Increase in temperature
